data.question: Does the split keep every test id

chunk_findings.detail: The stated split plan requires removing the offender’s baseline exception after the oversized file is split, but the manifest contains no change to `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. Given that `tests/test_shard_high_water.py` was over `[quality].max_file_bytes` and the ratchet was green before, it must have had a baseline line recording the old oversized allowance. Leaving that line in place means the thin facade can still grow back to over 30000 bytes without the size ratchet catching it, so the split does not actually enforce the new smaller size and violates [D-small-files-30k].
chunk_findings.title: tests/file_size_baseline.txt:tests/test_shard_high_water.py

chunk_findings.detail: The diff deletes the local `clone` fixture and imports only `_clone_fixture` from the new support module; it never binds that fixture as `clone` (no `from ... import _clone_fixture as clone` or `clone = _clone_fixture`). The first remaining test still requests `clone`, so running `pytest tests/test_shard_high_water.py::test_healthy_after_normal_use` errors during collection with `fixture 'clone' not found`. The `# noqa: F401` comment hides the unused import but does not make the fixture name match, so this is a behavior change from the stated no-behaviour split.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_shard_high_water.py:test_healthy_after_normal_use

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s manifest contains only the test/support files and no edit to `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. The split was filed because `tests/test_shard_high_water.py` was the size-ratchet offender over `[quality].max_file_bytes`; for the pre-split tree to have been green, that offender must have had a baseline entry. After moving the large trailing test block out, that baseline entry remains, so the ratchet still permits the old oversized baseline (or fails as a stale entry), violating the required cleanup [D-small-files-30k].
chunk_findings.title: tests/file_size_baseline.txt

chunk_findings.detail: The change splits the oversized test file but does not include the required cleanup of `tests/file_size_baseline.txt`. The stated intent says `tests/test_shard_high_water.py` was over the 30000-byte limit and that, after splitting, its baseline line must be deleted if present; since the file was over the limit and expected to keep the size ratchet green before the change, that baseline entry exists and remains in this change. Leaving the stale baseline entry violates [D-small-files-30k] and preserves a ratchet exception for a file that is no longer supposed to need one, allowing future growth to slip past the size check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/file_size_baseline.txt
